editorial:
Imagine being a small-town doctor who writes funny stories on the side just to put food on the table. That is exactly where you find Anton Chekhov in the summer of 1890. You get to see him struggle through his early days, using a pen name to make a bit of extra cash before the big shots in the literary world notice him. The vibe is very quiet and thoughtful, taking you back to a time of old letters, ink pots, and slow walks through the countryside. It is a grounded look at a man who is caught between his duty as a doctor and his passion for writing.

You will really appreciate how the movie shows the weight of success. While it is great to see him win awards and get praised by legends like Tolstoy, the real heart of the story is the pain he feels when he cannot save his own brother. The acting is steady and honest, though the pacing is a bit slow for people who like action. If you enjoy deep character studies, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the best way to keep this beautiful piece of history.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heavy note. After the death of his brother from tuberculosis, Anton is crushed by guilt. He feels like a failure because he is a doctor who could not save his own family. Instead of celebrating his fame and the love in his life, he chooses to pull away from everyone. He decides to leave his success behind to find a way to deal with his grief and his sense of duty.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about artists and historical biographies.
